title: Our offices peak on Tuesday–Thursday and sit mostly empty on Mondays and Fridays, so Denver could give back a floor
subtitle: Ten weeks of badge and desk-booking data show Denver HQ never used more than 612 of its 900 desks. People rate office days as worth the commute when their own team is in, which is a matter of coordination, not of desk count.
summary: Badge and desk-booking data for Denver HQ and Chicago show attendance concentrated on Tuesday–Thursday. Denver averages 42% desk utilisation and its busiest day in 10 weeks used 612 of 900 desks, so the floor 6 give-back option (worth about $1.1M a year) is viable if midweek demand is spread more evenly. Teams with anchor days are together 2.3× as often, and people rate office days as worth the commute when their team is there.
key_findings: Denver desk utilisation averages 42%, from 11% on Fridays to 62% on Wednesdays. Chicago averages 31%, peaking at 48%.
Denver's busiest day used 612 desks, which is 85% of four-floor capacity. Giving back floor 6 saves about $1.1M a year from 2027.
Teams with anchor days have at least half the team in on 63% of office days, compared with 27% for teams without (2.3×).
78% rated an office day as 'worth the commute' when 75%+ of their team was in, compared with 36% when under 25% was.
